steps.say: Muscle invasive bladder cancer needs chemotherapy before surgery. Combinations of cisplatin drugs add five to eight extra survivors in a hundred at five years. The drugs kill hidden spread while the bladder is still in place, so fit patients receive chemotherapy first and cystectomy after.
steps.tx: **Neoadjuvant cisplatin** (preoperative platinum chemotherapy) with accelerated **MVAC** (multi-agent MVAC regimen) or gemcitabine plus cisplatin confers a **5% to 8%** absolute overall **survival advantage** at **5 years** (five years) in muscle-invasive bladder cancer. The gain comes from eradicating micrometastases with the primary in situ, so fit cT2 to T4a patients receive chemotherapy first and cystectomy after.

vis.caption: Papillary tumour at cystoscopy; muscle invasion on TURBT staging leads to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Credit: Unknown, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: The standard operation removes the bladder with its neighbours. In men this takes the prostate, seminal vesicles, lower ureters, and regional nodes. In women it takes the urethra, uterus, ovaries, and front vaginal wall. Anything less leaves microscopic disease behind.
steps.tx: Standard **radical cystectomy** (complete bladder removal with neighbours) takes bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles, distal ureters, and regional nodes in men; the female **anterior pelvic exenteration** (extended cystectomy) takes bladder, urethra, uterus, ovaries, and anterior vaginal wall. The extent reflects local spread patterns, and lesser surgery leaves microscopic disease behind.

rows: Bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles, distal ureters, nodes
Bladder, urethra, uterus, ovaries, anterior vaginal wall
Match the operation to local spread patterns

steps.say: Node surgery has a numeric target. At least ten to fifteen nodes are cleared from both sides of the pelvis, covering the external iliac, internal iliac, and obturator groups. The count stages the patient and removes hidden spread, and higher yields are linked with better survival.
steps.tx: Bilateral pelvic **lymph node dissection** (systematic nodal clearance) should clear at least **10 to 15 nodes** (ten to fifteen) across external iliac, internal iliac (hypogastric), and **obturator nodes** (obturator fossa packets). The yield stages accurately and removes occult metastases, with higher counts linked to better survival. Token sampling of a few nodes understages the disease.

rows: At least 10 to 15 nodes, both sides
Accurate staging plus occult metastasis removal
Understages disease, linked with worse outcomes

steps.say: The simplest diversion is built from a short piece of small bowel. Fifteen to twenty centimetres of terminal ileum are taken well clear of the ileocaecal valve. Both ureters join one end and the other end forms a skin stoma. It leaks by design and remains the most dependable option for elderly patients.
steps.tx: The **ileal conduit** (**Bricker diversion**, incontinent ileal stoma) takes a **15 cm to 20 cm** length of terminal ileum **15 cm** above the ileocecal valve, joins both ureters to one end, with the other end matured as a skin stoma. Incontinent by design, it stays the most dependable diversion, especially for elderly or comorbid patients who cannot cope with a continent reservoir.

rows: 15 cm clear of the ileocecal valve
Both implanted into one end of the segment
Other end to skin, incontinent by design

steps.say: The continent option is built from more bowel. Fifty to sixty centimetres of ileum are opened, folded into a round low pressure reservoir, and joined to the native urethra. The patient then passes urine normally. It needs motivation and the ability to wash out mucus, so selection remains strict.
steps.tx: The **orthotopic neobladder** (**Studer pouch** or Hautmann reservoir) detubularizes **50 cm to 60 cm** of ileum into a low-pressure spherical reservoir from **detubularized ileum** (opened bowel refashioned without its tube shape), anastomosed directly to the native urethral stump for per-urethral voiding. It demands motivation, dexterity for mucus irrigation, and acceptance of possible self-catheterization for hypercontinence, so selection stays strict.

rows: 50 to 60 cm of ileum, detubularized and folded round
Direct anastomosis to native urethral stump
Per urethra from a low-pressure reservoir

steps.say: Bowel in the urinary tract produces a fixed pattern of salt disturbance. The segment soaks up ammonium and chloride while losing bicarbonate, producing an acid blood state with high chloride. Follow up therefore checks bicarbonate and kidney function for life, and daily alkali prevents bone and stone damage.
steps.tx: **Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis** (acid blood from chloride gain and bicarbonate loss) is the classic **electrolyte disturbance** after ileal or colonic diversions: segments reabsorb urinary ammonium and chloride in exchange for bicarbonate and sodium. Lifelong follow-up checks venous bicarbonate and renal function, and maintenance alkali prevents bone demineralization and stone formation.

rows: Bicarbonate and sodium to the urine
Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, chronic bicarbonate loss
Lifelong bicarbonate checks plus maintenance alkali

steps.say: Selected patients keep their bladders. A complete scraping of the tumour followed by combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy matches cystectomy survival in the right cases: a single T2 tumour, no swollen kidney, and no widespread flat cancer. The bladder then stays under lifelong watch, with removal held back for failure.
steps.tx: **Trimodal therapy** (bladder preservation triad) of maximal TURBT followed by concurrent **chemoradiotherapy** (combined chemotherapy plus radiotherapy) matches cystectomy survival in selected patients: solitary T2 tumours without hydronephrosis or extensive carcinoma in situ, with good bladder function. Surveillance is lifelong and unforgiving, with salvage cystectomy reserved for incomplete response or invasive recurrence.

vis.alt: Diagram of urinary tract obstruction sites with upstream hydronephrosis.
vis.caption: Hydronephrosis from obstruction rules out bladder preservation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Widespread disease has a new first line treatment. An antibody carrying a poison to Nectin-4 on cancer cells, paired with pembrolizumab, extends both the time without growth and overall survival. It has replaced platinum drugs for eligible patients, with skin and nerve side effects needing close watch.
steps.tx: **Enfortumab vedotin** (antibody-drug conjugate targeting **Nectin-4**, a cell-surface protein) combined with **pembrolizumab** extends the time without progression and overall survival when used first for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer. The pairing has displaced platinum chemotherapy for eligible patients, with skin toxicity and peripheral neuropathy as signature side effects to monitor.

rows: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer, first line
